key_insight: The paper proposes hierarchical alignment between EEG signals and text to support non-invasive brain-to-text communication. The provided abstract is incomplete, so its results and performance cannot be verified.
problem_solved: People with conditions such as locked-in syndrome, cerebral palsy, and dysarthria need alternative communication pathways, while many recent brain-to-text advances rely on bulky, costly neuroimaging equipment.
method: Use EEG as the brain-signal modality for a non-invasive brain-to-text interface, as indicated by the title.

impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the work highlights cross-modal alignment between noisy neural signals and language as a route toward more accessible assistive interfaces. Practical value depends on decoding accuracy, robustness, and user validation, none of which are reported in the supplied excerpt.
